title: Traffic glitch → warm strings
prompt:
Make a 30 s music bed for a TikTok ad at 30 fps.
Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 1440000 samples.
Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads). Fixed random seed.
Timing: 90 BPM (1 beat = 20 frames). Cues: frame 0 = urban hit; frame 300 = traffic cuts, strings swell; last beat = soft ending that fades to exactly 0.
Sound: [chaos: honks, sirens, stuttering hi-hats, bit-crushed noise] → [calm: slow legato strings, soft sub, gentle pulse at 90 BPM], key A minor.
Master: −14 LUFS integrated, true peak ≤ −1 dBTP.
You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and peak with ffmpeg ebur128, check the exact length, confirm the energy change lands on each cue frame, check the notes fit the chords, render a spectrogram and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.
notes: Runner-verified synthesis (numpy). Prompt describes creative intent; code is executable. WAV shipped as 32 kHz mono for Workers 5 MiB asset limit.
